overall_summary: Recent 7-day performance clearly demonstrates that speculative, immersive 'What If' scenarios applied to extreme space phenomena (e.g., dark planets, liquid diamond worlds, burning ice planets) and high-engagement biology/history comparisons (e.g., octopuses' three hearts, ancient animal lifespans) generate the highest views-per-day, likes-per-view, and active comment engagement. Straight declarative space facts underperform compared to interactive thought experiments. Growth strategy should pivot entirely toward immersive second-person hypothetical framing combined with extreme planetary or biological anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1025 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (970 views, 18 likes) dramatically outperform static declarative space facts within their first 7 days.
winning_patterns.action: Structure future space and science hooks entirely around immediate physical second-person hypotheticals ('What would happen to your body if you stepped onto...').

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (363 views, 19 likes) and 'Sharks Are OLDER Than Saturn's Rings?' (297 views, 18 likes) show exceptional engagement ratios compared to standard historical or psychological facts.
winning_patterns.action: Use counter-intuitive temporal comparisons and biological oddities that challenge conventional timelines or human anatomy.

weak_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' (11 views) or 'The Star Colder Than Ice' (82 views) published without an interactive premise stall out immediately.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid dry, textbook statements of fact; always anchor the concept to a tangible, visceral, or catastrophic scenario.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on internal brain hacks or psychological tricks (e.g., stopping songs stuck in your head, fake memories) gathered very low engagement (<70 views).
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize psychological trivia in favor of high-visual-potential space, geography, or cinematic animal survival topics.

next_video.concept: What happens to the human body if you stood unprotected on a rogue planet hurtling through interstellar space with no star?
next_video.opening_direction: Start in pitch blackness with sound design of freezing wind, asking the viewer: 'If you stood on a rogue planet drifting between stars, you wouldn't freeze to death instantly—something much stranger would happen to your blood first.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that because rogue planets retain deep geothermal heat from their core while their surface touches absolute zero, your front side would boil while your back side instantly shatters into glass.
next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' planetary immersion formula while introducing a completely fresh astronomical subject (rogue planets) distinct from previous diamond or ice planet topics.
fresh_topic_constraints: Must not mention diamond planets, ice planets, or Saturn.
Must use brand new rogue planet entity.
Must include active second-person physical consequence within the first 3 seconds.

experiment: Test a 15-second cinematic animal survival micro-story featuring an extreme deep-sea hydrothermal vent organism to measure if high-tension nature narratives can match the dominant space 'What If' engagement rates.
